findings.title: Stop returns before accepted jobs are handled
findings.explanation: Stop only closes stop and never waits on the worker WaitGroup. If Enqueue has accepted a buffered job, the worker can select the closed stop channel and return before reading that job, so Command.Shutdown can report success while the audit job was dropped.
findings.evidence: The requirement and usage context require Shutdown to wait for every accepted job. In run at line 6, once stop is closed both stop and input may be ready and select may choose stop; line 8 does not call q.wg.Wait. A concrete trigger is New, Enqueue(func(){record audit}), then Stop immediately: Stop returns without establishing that record ran. The bounded fix is to preserve draining semantics and wait for worker completion before Stop returns (and make repeated Stop behavior explicit if required).

findings.title: Parser discards escaped-separator semantics
findings.explanation: strings.Split(raw, ";") treats every semicolon as a rule separator, including a backslash-escaped one. The required input name=alpha\;beta;enabled=true is therefore split into three pieces instead of two, changing the first value and violating the format consumed by the migration loader.
findings.evidence: The requirement explicitly says a backslash escapes the following separator, and context/format.md says values may contain literal semicolons. At line 5, Parse splits before line 6 can filter empty rules; no escape state or unescaping/preservation logic exists. Trigger: Parse("name=alpha\\;beta;enabled=true") yields ["name=alpha\\", "beta", "enabled=true"] rather than ["name=alpha\\;beta", "enabled=true"]. The bounded fix is to scan raw while tracking backslash escape state, splitting only on unescaped semicolons and retaining the escaped separator in the value.

findings.title: Flag decoder no longer uses comma delimiters
findings.explanation: strings.Fields splits on whitespace instead of commas and leaves commas attached to tokens. For the documented input --region=us, --verbose it returns ["--region=us,", "--verbose"], so the child receives a malformed first argument; an item containing internal spaces is also split into multiple arguments.
findings.evidence: The requirement and context/docs.md define a comma-delimited value with surrounding whitespace ignored per item. Line 5 uses strings.Fields, and line 7 only filters already-separated fields, so it cannot remove the delimiter or preserve item boundaries. Trigger: DecodeFlags("--region=us, --verbose") produces a trailing comma in the first argument. The bounded fix is to split on comma, trim each item, and omit empty items.

findings.title: Concurrent retries race and can create multiple charges
findings.explanation: The mutex protecting the idempotency check and charge creation was removed. Concurrent CreatePayment calls with the same key can both miss seen, compute different or duplicate payment IDs, write the shared map concurrently, and increment charges more than once; concurrent map access can also panic.
findings.evidence: The requirement requires concurrent retries with one original payment and one charge. Checkout forwards directly to CreatePayment, and lines 16 and 19-21 perform the check, ID allocation, map write, and charge increment without synchronization. Trigger: two goroutines call Checkout("k", cents) at the same time (the supplied barrier hooks make the pre-write interleaving explicit); both pass line 16 before either writes line 20, so charges can become 2 and the two returned IDs need not match. The bounded fix is to restore a mutex or equivalent atomic critical section covering the check and creation, while retaining Reset for test-store reset.
